title: Akita — 秋田
goal: Build common food words from familiar characters and new rice/thing characters.

cards.title: A New Prefecture with a Food Connection

blocks.text: Akita is both a prefecture and its capital city's name. Akita City is associated with the Kanto Festival, whose lanterns form large displays. We will use the wider rice/meal setting for language practice, without teaching festival numbers or schedules.
**秋田でご飯を食べます。** あきたで ごはんを たべます。 — I eat a meal in Akita.
ご飯 is introduced with its reading immediately; the next cards explain its spelling. A meal scene extends eating/buying from Aomori. We can add vocabulary without restarting the grammar of を and で.

items: **Character:** 秋 · **Meaning/reading:** autumn; あき, シュウ · **Radical and components:** 禾, のぎへん, beside 火 · **Role:** Assisted encounter, including review of Hokkaido's seasonal wording. Modern shapes are not the entire historical explanation.
**Character:** 田 · **Meaning/reading:** cultivated field/rice paddy; た, デン · **Radical and components:** 田, た; enclosed grid, a field-derived whole character · **Role:** Formal study.

blocks.text: **秋田 / あきた** is the whole location name. 秋 + 田 gives spelling glosses, not a verified story of its naming. 禾 differs from 木 by the short top stroke: notice this shape from 私. Grain, fire and field imagery can aid memory while useful words control the actual reading.
**田んぼ / たんぼ — rice paddy; 田 / た — cultivated field.** The kana ending belongs to the common word. You can recognise 田 in 秋田 without treating all the word's spoken sounds as new on readings.
**田んぼに水があります。** たんぼに みずが あります。 — There is water in the rice paddy.

This sentence describes an imagined paddy photograph. It does not claim that paddies always contain standing water. The existence pattern is review: place に, thing が, あります. 田 is a whole field radical; its internal lines are not separate numbers or mouths added to produce its meaning.

**米 / こめ — rice, especially uncooked grain; お米 / おこめ — the same word with a polite prefix.** 米 is its own radical, こめ. Notice the central cross and spreading strokes as a complete grain-related shape.
**店で米を買います。** みせで こめを かいます。 — I buy rice at the shop.

お does not create another independent kanji word. 米 is ベイ/マイ in other compounds; today's priority is こめ. Do not invent a sound by adding 八 and 十. Cooking and eating lead to another everyday word on the next card; the same material can be named differently in different contexts.
**ご飯 / ごはん — cooked rice; meal.** 飯 has **食** in its left-side food form **飠**, しょくへん, plus **反**, a historical sound component. Food is a useful meaning clue; the entire word is learned as ごはん.
**ご飯を食べます。** ごはんを たべます。 — I eat rice / a meal.

In **朝ご飯** later, ご飯 clearly means a meal. In a bowl beside other food it may mean cooked rice specifically. Compare 米を買います (buy uncooked rice) and ご飯を食べます (eat cooked rice/a meal). This is a useful everyday distinction, not a claim that every dictionary context is mutually exclusive.

cards.title: 物: A Thing Inside Common Words

blocks.text: **物 / もの — thing; 食べ物 / たべもの — food; 飲み物 / のみもの — drink/beverage.** Radical **牛** in its left **牜**, うしへん, plus **勿**, a historical sound component. The component does not make every 物 a cow.
食べ物 keeps 食べ and adds 物; 飲み物 keeps 飲み and adds 物. These are nouns, while 食べます/飲みます are actions. Notice the different kana endings.
**これは飲み物です。** これは のみものです。 — This is a drink.
You can recognise 牛 as a component before formally studying the standalone animal word in Fukushima. Encountering a shape and studying its word are different learning events.

items: **Word:** 食べる · **Reading:** たべる · **Meaning/category:** action: eat
**Word:** 食べ物 · **Reading:** たべもの · **Meaning/category:** noun: food
**Word:** 飲む · **Reading:** のむ · **Meaning/category:** action: drink
**Word:** 飲み物 · **Reading:** のみもの · **Meaning/category:** noun: beverage

blocks.text: **水は飲み物です。** みずは のみものです。 — Water is a drink.
**魚は食べ物です。** さかなは たべものです。 — Fish is food, in our food scene.

A living fish in a nature scene is still described with います. Calling an item food in a meal context does not change the earlier person/animal-versus-thing existence lesson into a mechanical rule about every fish.
**これは何ですか。** これは なんですか。 — What is this?
**米です。** こめです。 — It is rice.
**それは食べ物ですか。** それは たべものですか。 — Is that food?
**はい、食べ物です。** はい、たべものです。 — Yes, it is food.

These questions reuse 何, これ/それ and ですか. The question word's form is なん in 何ですか. A learner need not identify every cooking method to answer an elementary category question. Keep objects clear in the exercise image so that only one category is intended.
Imagine a shop sells apples for **三百円 / さんびゃくえん** in our stated two-apple purchase. This is the total, not a unit price.
**りんごを二つ買いました。三百円でした。** りんごを ふたつ かいました。さんびゃくえんでした。 — I bought two apples. It was 300 yen.

Here **Nでした** is explicitly introduced as the polite past of **Nです** for a price/identification. It differs from the い-adjective ending in 安かったです. We can say **この飲み物は水です**, this drink is water, and **水でした**, it was water, without treating でした as a verb's ました ending.
**いただきます** is the customary phrase before eating; **ごちそうさまでした** is said after a meal. These were taught in Hachinohe and now return naturally.
**秋田でご飯を食べました。水も飲みました。** あきたで ごはんを たべました。みずも のみました。 — I ate a meal in Akita. I also drank water.
**店で食べ物と飲み物を買いました。** みせで たべものと のみものを かいました。 — I bought food and drinks at a shop.
と joins the noun categories; も adds an action about water. Cultural courtesy is practised in context rather than scored as trivia about a particular festival.

items: Read 秋田 and 田んぼ. **Answer:** あきた; たんぼ.
Which taught word names uncooked rice? **Answer:** 米 / こめ.
What two common meanings does ご飯 have? **Answer:** cooked rice; meal.
Read 食べ物 and 飲み物. **Answer:** たべもの; のみもの.
Which component links 飯 with 食べる? **Answer:** 食/飠.
Read 水でした and 安かったです. **Answer:** みずでした, it was water; やすかったです, it was inexpensive. They use different predicate patterns.

blocks.text: 秋田 is あきた. 秋 is assisted; 田 is formal study. 田んぼ is a rice paddy, 米 is uncooked rice, ご飯 is cooked rice or a meal. 食べ物/飲み物 are nouns made from familiar action stems plus 物. A price/identification noun can use でした in a polite past report; an い-adjective uses its own ending.
**Recall task:** “I bought food and drinks at a shop.” **Model:** 店で食べ物と飲み物を買いました。 Continue to Kakunodate and write a short memory of the trip.
